{"source_passages":[{"id":"E118-C","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA, 
and host or bovine immunoglobulins that originate from ascites or cell culture serum. The problem of contaminants of 
animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine 
immunoglobulins pose three different purification problems: albumin because of its abundance; transferrin because of its 
similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.","quote_sha256":"b961c80dda07292a0520ff7fda7116e0af15de4498923da84a9a09cce7336ba4","page_text_start":541,"page_text_end":1292}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E119-AH","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification","quote":"Albumin and transferrin","quote_sha256":"c083fa89230d3d7cd7cc963daeee26692ab7fc3397e3c24aac14c5a7db185051","page_text_start":1382,"page_text_end":1405},{"id":"E119-I","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification","quote":" After an IEX purification, albumin and transferrin can be present if their charge properties are similar to those of \nthe target antibody. In some cases, it might be possible to optimize pH and elution conditions in the IEX step to \nimprove the separation between the antibody and the contaminants (Appendix 9).","quote_sha256":"8c5889325bb188941f1a6ebace48bfa19be64eea938525ddb6fe835a1d313fd4","page_text_start":1682,"page_text_end":1994}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E118-USE","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"For many applications at laboratory scale, contaminant molecules are not always a significant problem. Affinity \nchromatography (AC) will provide sufficient purity and, as long as the presence of any minor contaminants does not \ninterfere with the intended application, the purified sample can be used directly.","quote_sha256":"353719de9177ea9d6b00bb5aaac1470a50ea3a083db5f615a4e9284091a1fb2e","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":311}]}

selection of optimal binding and elution conditions. Figure 4.1 shows an example of chromatography media screening 
of a mouse monoclonal antibody on different HIC media prepacked in HiTrap 1 mL columns. In this case, the optimal 
medium for purification was HiTrap Phenyl HP.","quote_sha256":"b7f9b22e4a4b994c309bba80c118736640dea30ad3fbef4593ac2239ac5f8dcb","page_text_start":985,"page_text_end":1380},{"id":"E119-BI","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Difficulties have also been encountered when murine monoclonal antibodies are the target molecule. between the physical characteristics of the target antibody and the contaminants require careful selection and 
optimization to find the most suitable chromatography technique for purification. Both HIC and IEX can be used.","quote_sha256":"dba348e8e3dd9c320f962ceed1025882e42d5781aeddfdd63f67c570d779a634","page_text_start":432,"page_text_end":772},{"id":"E119-S","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":" The hydrophobicity of proteins is difficult to predict. hydrophobicities (e.g., using HiTrap HIC Selection Kit) to find the medium that gives optimal results.","quote_sha256":"6741c581e5bc9fdfd5aad6f728f5e9e5dc438d26155cd1a0bde2846ffd1302a8","page_text_start":773,"page_text_end":984},{"id":"E119-B","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Co-purification of host or bovine immunoglobulins is a problem associated with any affinity purification of antibodies
